Have always had a soft spot for this musical, it's Liza at her BEST. Well made, memorable Characters and overall entertaining!

history.title: Mortdecai [Blu-ray + Digital HD]
history.review_title: If you like Johnny Depp - this film is for you
history.text: This is a true oddball ( typical )Johnny Depp film - you either like it or hate it. Part Comedy, Drama and frankly plain weirdness adds to the fun!
Well advertised , this film ranks right up there with the Blair Witch Project. If you like shaky Camera Pictures, a bad story, bad acting and overall bad everything - this film is for you!

history.title: Matinee
history.text: Few People like this film - I love it! Not only is it about Horror Films of the 60's - it makes fun of all the paranoia that took place in this country during the cuban missle crisis. Most of my friends thought it was lame, but I will always love it for what it is - a cute little ditty about life under pressure and the fun of going to the movies!

history.title: Gattaca [Blu-ray]
history.text: This was one of those Utopian Films that didn't get a lot of recognition. It should have, - well made, well acted, great story! It's hard to put it into a category, ( it's NOT lightsabers and spaceships )mainly it's political and it sure makes it's point! This is a film that makes you think and question - isn't that what great films are supposed to do?

history.title: True Blood
history.text: Little surprise it got cancelled, this show went from cute to stupid to religious. Charlaine Harris isn't much of a writer - her first 3 books were lighthearted fun that seemed to be more for the Teenie Genre than serious fiction after that I quit reading her garbage! HBO picked it up , and I give them credit for doing a fairly well done job on screen. However - they managed to screw it up, too. Good Ideas , bad writing. It tried to cover the whole fantasy Genre - everything included. Great Actors, but the writers really lost it. Religion got in the way - and I don't care if it's christian, or voodoo, or muslim - it's all crap! Bill getting killed was not much of a surprise - they really had no place else to go. Maybe they made him into a vampire jesus in their own minds? I really don't care, just glad this comedy is over. Too bad- this could have been really good, but it really went down hill .

I thought discrimination was against the law. Worf was a pit mix - unwanted , unloved I got him when he was 6 weeks old, afraid of his own shadow. He grew up to be a terrific dog. My friends had purebreds, - again , loving, sweet dogs. These dogs got a bad wrap because of people. - Mostly the worst kind. Those morons MAKE these dogs vicious, and bite for bite your Shepard is a lot more dangerous ( look it up). It's not okay to descriminate among people, it's okay to put a breed of dog down, though. What kind of society are we living in? We need laws to prosecute the vicious individuals who turn these dogs into killers , because they are too cowardly to be the vicious animals they were born to be themselves. ( Wanna be tough guys who lack the guts!) And a breed that is just a dog pays the price. Tell you what - I have a dog , a loving, caring canine and what scares me is that he could be classified as "vicious" at any given time. He is considered "Property", not family! Isn't it time we revoked these laws and looked at reality? Just a few days ago a Pomeranian was beaten to death and left with a note " Quoting : lol , haha we beat him to death". Just who are the real vicious animals here?

history.title: CSI: Crime Scene Investigation: The Final Season
history.text: Little surprise it got cancelled - they turned it into a soap opera with all the "human baggage". Basically they seem to have run out of ideas ( or headlines) and got into the human aspect of the thing. Not a good turn , I liked the "overblown" methods, the grittiness and the special effects - if I want to watch a soap opera - daytime TV is loaded with those. It's been a fun 15 years, but I can't say I'm sorry to see it go the way of the Dodo!

history.title: Tut
history.text: Nothing to brag about, good actors, special effects that are mediocre, bad writing and historically accurate? No one really knows do they, so you can feel free to improvise , I suppose. I am not a historian , but the whole thing was dragged , the battle scenes not so believable and the love scenarios overcooked. To say the least I was disappointed .Wish I hadn't bought it - I am stuck with the fiasco. Acting was nothing short of really great - but the writing lacked a royal root!

history.title: Dark Kingdom - The Dragon King
history.text: Growing up with Siegfried I figured someone had to make a movie. - I liked it better than I thought I would. It's not great, but well made , has good acting and they stuck to the story. What more could you want?

history.title: Into the Woods
history.text: Honestly I bought this because of Johnny Depp and all he has is a bit part. It's okay - I grew up in the Grimm Brothers Neighborhood , it's kind of fun to watch them lob all the fairy tales together, on the other hand it's kind of sad to see them butchered like this. But overall it was well made!

history.title: Jurassic World [Blu-ray]
history.text: This was by far the worst re- make I have ever seen. Why did they even bother? Mediocre acting, no writing worth bragging about, too much dialogue and special effects that were few and far between. This is a classic example of making money off someone else with no effort on your part. There was nothing original in this movie. These guys should be ashamed!

No Elena? Well and good - this whole soap opera thing was entertaining and all, but I could well do without Elena Gilbert. They are Vampires - do something with it. Instead they kept focusing on the "love " - bad choice. They had an opportunity to make a good show really great, but failed and it looks like Damon is leaving the show. If that really is the case , they will sink like the Titanic and you can attribute that to bad writing, not bad acting! If you love soaps so much watch Day time TV, if you love Vampires this show had a great go at it. I never did watch if for the love interest, I loved the make-up and the blood. And Damon was one of the Best. ( So was Caroline). I would hate to see it end like this just because the writers can't get their act together!

history.title: Game of Thrones: Season 5 [Blu-ray + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Two wrongs don't make one right
history.text: Still love that show - I hope they keep it going. I was a year late getting it on DVD, so I already knew about some of the spoilers. Everyone was up in arms about the rape of Sansa Stark, yet nobody seemed to be bothered by the fact that Shireen was killed by her own father being blindsided by religion! Did I miss something here ? In the dark ages women were sold to men to do with as they pleased ( in some places they still are) and Sansa had the option to get out - she declined . Shireen (who did not have a choice) was burned at the stake- by her father, no less -yet I did not hear a peep about that atrocity. Are we as a country so steeped in religion that this is acceptable?

history.title: Young Dracula - The BBC Series: Complete Seasons 1, 2, 3, 4 (54 Episodes) - 12 DVD Collection
history.text: I love all things Vampires - not sorry I bought this, I just wish I had known it's made for kids. Cute in a way, but not really what I wanted. Next time I will pay better attention to the previews. Well made, just not what I was expecting. If you love Vampires like I do and you have Kids - you will like this!

Well made, great acting - good cast. A few of these Actors and Actresses wound up on Game of Thrones, given the talent, it was a great choice. Honestly I wasn't expecting much going into this, but was pleasantly surprised and hurried to watch all four episodes. If you like History, a good storyline, good acting and good writing - don't miss out on this.

Honestly I bought this because of Johnny Depp.- He only had a very small part it turns out - but I was NOT disappointed with the movie, far from it. Very few people I know of had ever even heard of it - too bad. Well made, well acted - not some cheap stupid remake of a comic book or the zillionth part to something started 30 years ago. I really enjoyed it and am looking forward to part 2.Not sure how little ones would take to it - but it's a fun film and I am so very glad it's in my collection! I have loved animals all my life and this is one of those films that touches upon that, real or fake - it's a great movie!

history.title: The Vampire Diaries: The Complete Eighth and Final Season
history.review_title: Talk about a great show going to hell , literally , pun intended!
history.text: Wow - can we spell FUBAR? Season 7 was bad enough, they had a great story to follow and totally destroyed it. Season 8 is so bad I had to watch it basically in fast forward. It's not the actors faults - they were as good as ever , but the writers seem to have all been lobotomized. No surprise the show got cancelled, season 8 is laughable to say the least. Well it closed out the series for me, but I am so sorry I wasted money on this hell bend ( literally), no brain idiocy!

history.title: CSI: Cyber - Season 1
history.text: You can't fault the actors , but the writers leave a lot to be desired. It's kind of a personal drama/ rehab the bad guys/not knowing what to do with it .After watching 2 whole episodes - I wasn't surprised it got cancelled. Mediocre, slightly above average TV, but just slightly. It proofs that just jumping on the bandwagon doesn't cut the mustard. Too bad, with just a little better writing effort it could have been a great show. (By the way I bought the whole thing and did watch it and it did NOT improve past those first two episodes!)

history.title: The Hanging Tree
history.text: At last, this classic Delmer DAVES western comes to life through Warner Archive Collection, as we all expected, in widescreen and gorgeous Technicolor. Forget all the previous european editions in fullscreen and soft colours, and buy this one at once. Gary COOPER has never been so good, as Dr FRAIL, so is the rest of the cast (wonderful Karl MALDEN...)A must for moviebuffs of the 50's !

history.title: Lost Horizon (1973)
history.text: I had read so many bad reviews about this film, that it arose my curiosity, considering the fact that it was produced...40 years ago. Should it stand the test of time ? Well, to my opinion, the answer is....YES. Of course, it looks a bit dated now, the peace and love trend of the late sixties being gone now long ago ( forever ? ) I think that the main problem are the songs,because as good as they are, they seem out of place, being not really needed. As a matter of fact, this could have been a very decent film, but not as a musical. Nevertheless, it has many beautiful numbers, even if Hermes PAN choreography is particularly uninspired, and despite its many flaws, it does not deserve such a bad reputation. THIS IS A MUSICAL, A FAIRY TALE, very much like BRIGADOON, so why try to explain it ? JUST ENJOY !!!!!!

history.title: Diane
history.text: There was a time, long ago, when MGM was ruling its kingdom in Culver City, California, sparing no expenses when it came to movie business. We have a fine example here, with this 1955 film, the french court of the 16th century had been so lavishly recreated, that you can't believe your eyes...The scenery, the costumes and the music by the great Miklos ROZSA are just perfect. The acting is quite good too, especially the scenes between Lana TURNER and Marisa PAVAN, even if a very young Roger MOORE is far less convincing as king HENRY II. Of course, being french, I noticed some historical mistakes ( I don't think that king FRANCOIS 1st died of battle wounds) but does it really matter ? This Warner Collection release is a real treat with gorgeous colors, and full stereo sound.....Don't hesitate, you won't be sorry to get this DVD !

history.title: Athena (Remastered)
history.text: i had never heard of this film before, but I was not disappointed at all. It's refreshing and funny all the way, not all fashioned like big budgets musicals of 1954 at MGM, I mean "Brigadoon" or "Rose Marie".....Of course, the storyline won't give you a headache, but who cares when Jane POWELL, Debbie REYNOLDS and Vic DAMONE are involved. The music is good and the songs are a treat, in stereo sound on this Archive Collection DVD. We even get all the deleted numbers as a bonus, with Edmond PURDOM singing with a strong baritone voice to Jane POWELL !!!!

history.title: Beneath The 12-mile Reef
history.text: AT LAST ! Almost 60 years after its first release in France, and a following of bootleg and fuzzy pan and scan video treatment, this wonderful and underrated film comes to life again, through Twentieth Century Fox Archives collection, who apparently found back their lost copyright. Forget all the previous old DVD versions, and buy this one at once, you won't regret it. The image is clean and sharp as a razor, the colors are beautiful, and the Florida sunsets never looked better. This DVD ratio is 16/9 anamorphic, with a correct 2.55.1 ratio, and full stereo sound. Thank you, Fox, and don't get discouraged, there many others CinemaScope pictures, we are waiting for....

history.title: Track of the Cat (Special Collector's Editon)
history.text: This is indeed a very strange film, first by its cinematography, trying to avoid any lush colour, in any scene, mostly in the house, but outside too, with the exception of the flaming red jacket worn by Robert Mitchum, making a striking contrast with the snowy landscape all around. The screenplay seems to look more like a Eugene O'NEIL drama like "Desire Under the elms", with mixed characters, leaded by a rather dominating mother, and a weak father mostly interested in the bottle ! It's most unusual to watch a film in Warnercolor...in black and white, but William WELLMAN did it, and it still works, with some beautiful scenes, like the burrying of the son.

history.title: King Richard and the Crusaders
history.text: There is not much to say from this low-budgeted copy of MGM 's "Knights of the Round Table", except that it's in Cinemascope and Warnercolor ! The acting is poor, to say the least ( Even the great George SANDERS seems bored as Richard the Lion ) , the dialogue is terrible, and the cardboard looking sets don't help at all . The only asset to this picture is the music by Max STEINER, one of the best composers of Hollywood classics.

history.title: Guys and Dolls [Blu-ray]
history.text: There was a time, long ago, when Hollywood producers spared no expenses when it came to lavish ( and sometimes ludicrous ) recreations of Broadway stage musicals. Darryl Zanuck was one of them at Fox, along with Arthur FREED at the MGM lot. But it was a far more risky business for an independant Producer like Samuel Goldwyn to produce "GUYS AND DOLLS", with actors unable to sing and dance, and a director most famous for elaborate screenplays and dialogues in intellectual films. Well !!!!!!! What do you know ? It works !!!!!! Even not being Mario LANZA, Marlon BRANDO's voice is quite pleasant, so is Jean SIMMONS'. the choreography by Michael KIDD is inspired, the costumes by Irene SHARAFF and the sets by Oliver SMITH first rate too.. All this is carefully controlled by Joe MANKIEWICZ, who proves again what a great director is is.

history.title: Young at Heart
history.review_title: IT WAS A VERY GOOD YEAR
history.text: Doris DAY, Frank SINATRA, Robert KEITH, Dorothy MALONE, Elizabeth FRASER, Ethel BARRYMORE, Frank FERGUSON, Alan HALE Jr, Gig YOUNG, Lonnie CHAPMAN, believe it or not, all these talented people were starring in a small budgeted picture in 1954 called " YOUNG AT HEART", named after Frankie's hit of the period. The 3 Tuttle sisters are gorgeous, Sinatra is stunning as usual, playing a touching yet irritating, born loser, while Doris DAY is just the opposite ! There are lots of classic songs sung by the two stars, no sex or drugs or booze, here ( of course, this is 1954...) but it'a very pleasant film, cleverly directed by Gordon DOUGLAS. This DVD edition by Olive is presented in widescreen ratio, with a much better image than the previous edition of 2002 by Artisan, in full screen version.

history.title: Musicals Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: Well, this is really a first rate presentation of 3 big MGM musicals and a mild WB one. Indeed, as much as I love Doris DAY and Howard KEEL, "Calamity Jane" can't compete with "Kiss me Kate" and the rest, and David Butler is no Minnelli, Alas...However, the image is really crisp and the Technicolor is ....vibrant, as it should be ! The first complaint I would mention is the cardboard set used to store the 4 blurays, it's not very practical to take out the BD discs from a very narrow sleeve, you have to wipe the fingerprints on the edge of the BD quite often. The second complaint is about the bonuses : the 1948 travelogue about Manhattan has been trimmed from a 20 mn duration to a mere...5 minutes on the "KISS ME KATE" bluray, and the juke box selection on "Singin in the rain" is missing as well !

history.title: The Prince and the Showgirl
history.text: This film is a real disappointment, the stage play by Terence RATTIGAN being quite dated by now, and the very prudish direction by Laurence OLIVIER doesn't help at all the story to come up. There is not much chemistry between the two stars, but I guess the fault is on OLIVIER, whose performance is stiff and ridiculous throughout the picture. How could one fall in love with such a bully ? Marilyn is quite good here, but it's all wasted by the dulliness of the director....

history.title: The Quiet Man (60th Anniversary Special Edition) [Blu-ray]
history.text: This makes a perfect addition to a St. Patrick's Day movie marathon. The charming tale of going home again. And the quirky village characters make it all the more enjoyable. Make it an annual tradition in your home!

history.title: Disney Princess - A Christmas of Enchantment [DVD]
history.text: This DVD added a special Princess flavor to our holiday season. Some of the stories may be " lifted" or "recycled" from other Disney films, but they were still very enjoyable.

history.title: It Happened to Jane
history.text: For being generations removed from the current acting style, I've always found Doris Day's acing to be fresh, spontaneous & surprisingly modern. This lesser known Doris Day film is just as sweet & innocent as many of her others. I'm not sure why this one is somewhat forgotten. It has all the charm of "The Thrill Of It All" & "With Six, You Get Eggroll". Doris even sings 2 songs! And don't get me started on that nifty wood-paneled station wagon. I want one!

history.title: Ratatouille (Two-Disc Blu-ray/DVD Combo)
history.text: As a HUGE Disney fan, I'm ashamed to say I walked out of RATATOUILLE in the theatre. However, upon 2nd viewing years later, I have to say it is far more charming & clever than I remember. It's a refreshing departure from the traditional Princess/Fairy Tale" genre.

history.title: Disney's Timeless Tales, Vol. 1 - The Prince and the Pauper/Three Little Pigs/The Tortoise and the Hare [DVD]
history.text: A perfect addition to your family's collection. These cartoons are "pre-blockbusters" (like "The Incredibles", "Tangled" & "Wreck-It Ralph") and have that charm & simplicity Walt really strived for. Wonderful!

history.title: Freaky Friday
history.text: I had the privilege of briefly meeting Jamie Lee Curtis while this movie was opening. She's a smart, sweet, charming woman who delivers a great performance here. I think I enjoyed this remake as much as the original with Jodie Foster. Watch them BOTH and YOU decide!

history.title: Mommie Dearest (Hollywood Royalty Edition)
history.review_title: Timeless classic of a timeless woman!
history.text: This should be required watching for every film buff & gay man (or is that redundant? Lol) Faye Dunaway delivers a stellar performance of Joan Crawford. Some call it "over the top" and I agree. But that's what makes this guilty pleasure so pleasurable. It's NOT fact. Her life cannot be that one-sided. But for entertainment value, it's a must-see!

history.title: Blades of Glory [Blu-ray]
history.text: Will Ferrell is a modern Jerry Lewis. His performances are always fresh & spontaneous. BLADES OF GLORY is no exception. And with a superior cast (John Heder, Amy Poehler & Will Arnett) this is comic GOLD!

history.title: Brother Bear / Brother Bear 2 (3-Disc Special Edition) [Blu-ray / DVD]
history.review_title: Nice movie, but "Special Features" WON'T PLAY on Blu-ray
history.text: Anyone else having problems playing the Special Features on the Blu-ray disc? My discs (the original & the replacement) BOTH won't play the Special Features. The Blu-ray player just whirrs for about 20 seconds, then goes back to the Special Features Menu.

history.title: The Judy Garland Show, Vol. 1
history.review_title: Fan of Judy, but the show? Not so much
history.text: Although Judy Garland is one of my favorite performers, I found "The Judy Garland Show" to be lacking. Not enough Judy. And when Judy was on, she seemed off and awkward. Part of this I know had to do with her insecurities, but it's so much more evident in this show than in movie roles or even concert footage. I know the rest of the season is available, but I won't be buying them. In fact, I'll be reselling this one.

history.title: Diana Ross: Live In Central Park
history.text: I remember seeing this ill-fated concert on TV in the '80's. I was SO happy to see it available! And it does not disappoint. Miss Ross performance is, as always, PERFECTION! But her reaction to the impending storm & torrential rains makes me idolize her even more. It's a hoot! And the fact that this was done at a time when live TV was still quite young makes this all the more of a feat. LOVE it!

history.title: Planet of the Apes: Legacy Collection [Blu-ray]
history.text: Not only do you get all original 5 PLANET OF THE APES movies on blu-ray, but they've been packaged & reproduced with style & fun. Each disc stars with a CGI orangutan briefly telling you "inferior humans" the significance & history of the movie's release. Clever, humorous & well-done. Not to mention the menus are very well animated. Plus the picture & sound are crisp & clear. GREAT JOB!

history.title: Cinderella II: Dreams Come True / Cinderella III: A Twist In Time [Blu-ray]
history.text: This collection is worth getting for CINDERELLA 3. It's clever & well-done. CINDERELLA 2 is much more childish and feels like the "straight to video" films that Disney can sometimes make.
I'd love to see MORE pairings from this dynamic duo. Their timing & chemistry remind me of the great comic teams (Abbott & Costello, Lewis & Martin, etc).

history.title: Everybody Loves Raymond: Season 6 [DVD]
history.review_title: One of the best family comedies in history.
history.text: I was raised on "I Love Lucy", "Laverne & Shirley" & "The Andy Griffith Show" so my TV tastes run to more well-written, family-centric shows. This series is one of the top of the "modern era". ("Roseanne", "Friends" & "Will & Grace" being some others.) Hands down FAVORITE episode of this season was the Thanksgiving episode, "Older Women". OMG!

history.title: The Addams Family - The Complete Series
history.text: I really liked watching "The Addams Family" as a kid. I even enjoyed the movie remakes. But nothing compares to the original, And to have all the 3 seasons in one collection for this price is a great value! I enjoy popping it in and watching a few.

history.title: Meet Me in St. Louis [Blu-ray]
history.text: Judy Garland, Margaret O'Brien & a score to die for. What more could you ask for? Oh yeah, in glorious new Blu-ray. This has always been a favorite movie of mine. SO glad to see many of our old classics being transferred to Blu-ray! Get it & watch the antics of the Smith Family with your family.

history.title: Marilyn Monroe: Classic 9 Film Collection [Blu-Ray]
history.text: This Blu-ray pack is a steal! Plus it features some of Monroe's greatest work. Excellent deal.

history.title: Mom: Season 1
history.review_title: Can't believe I love a Chuck Lorre show!
history.text: I never liked Chuck Lorre's "Two and 1/2 Men", so I was shocked to discover how much I liked his "Mom"! Very few shows can be irreverent and intelligent at the same time. And the way this show handles addiction recovery is hilarious, insightful and touching.

history.title: The First Wives Club
history.text: Classic film that still holds up today. And what a cast!

targets.title: Winnie The Pooh: Springtime With Roo [Blu-ray]

history.title: World Without End [VHS]
history.text: Those looking for some sort of deep meaning underlying the film will likely be disappointed but if you are looking for a great evening of 1950's popcorn fare this is it. In fact despite some of its drawbacks it still has something that leaves one with the feeling that the whole film is a whole lot better than the sum of the parts - one of those that you can't quite place your finger on why you like it so much. Unfortunately, people tend to keep reviewing these films through the lens of today's high budgets and often over the top special effects. Folks when this flick was made computers were the size of large offices, gasoline was around 30 cents a gallon and jet airline service had been around for only four years - get some perspective. This movie gets points just for nostalgia value alone. Oh, and please don't go by what the fellow below with the 'sickening' review said - he obviously has some greater issues to deal with and is likely the type ready to trample all over your fun because it doesn't fit into some perverse Politically Correct mold. Enjoy the Movie!

history.title: Ender's Game [Blu-ray + DVD + Digital HD]
history.review_title: Enjoyable movie for non-pedantic sci fi fans
history.text: Pros: It's a space based sci-fi movie that is not star trek or star wars it isn't a remake The pace of the film was pretty good Good production value Liked the score Cons Characters are not particularly engaging - not sure if it's the actors or the fact that there's not enough time to flesh them out. Despite close to two hours I found that the film seemed to breeze by. Sometimes this is the mark of a really good movie; in this case I felt like the film was over before you got a chance to really get into it. I don't generally like to review a film based on the source novel as I believe it an unfair comparison. That said, I do think they should have done a better job of explaining certain things such as why Rackham is still alive and make it more obvious that battle school lasted several years. Overall I liked the movie and I'd say it's somewhere between 3 and 4 stars. Overall mixed feelings about the movie

history.title: Jack and The CuckooClock Heart [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Interesting film that doesn't follow a typical narrative
history.text: First off; as many reviewers have noted this film is not for the young kids - I think they would find it hard to follow and largely unsatisfying as it doesn't follow a typical hollywood style animated movie arc. There is no real 'lesson' in the film for kids to absorb. As for the innuendo stuff....I don't think little kids would even register the meaning in most cases so I don't see that as a strong mark against the film. For most adults I think this film will likely be either a hit or miss with little gray area in between. I enjoyed it because it is visually interesting but the story, while also having its own charm, seems a little scattered. Without spoiling anything, there doesn't seem to be a clear motivation for the main character's actions at the end (which can be interpreted as bittersweet) and much is left for viewer interpretation (at least that's my impression on first viewing). If you are an animation afficionado it's worth a watch.

history.title: Moon Zero Two
history.text: This is another space western complete with saloon brawl and moon canyon gunfight! Being something of an old scifi aficionado I was surprised that I hadn't heard of this film before. Hammer clearly put a fair amount of money into it and I think the overall art direction and production value is quite good for its time. I liked Olsen's performance as the wry astronaut - I've seen him elsewhere and that style seems to be his forte. Catherina Von Schell had little to do but looked nice doing it - except for the wig that is. My only gripes would be the overbearing soundtrack and the introductory cartoon which is silly, has an ugly art style and doesn't fit the film. a nice film for a rainy saturday afternoon.

history.title: Interstellar (Blu-ray + DVD Combo Pack)
history.review_title: competently produced science fiction film but not the 2001 of this generation. (This review has spoilers)
history.text: I wanted to be blown away by this film but it simply wasn't to be. Perhaps I simply allowed myself to get caught up in the hype and overblown expectations. It has plenty going for it theoretically. big name director, well known physicist as a science consultant, decent enough actors, big budget and yet... It has impressive visuals but it feels like the story doesn't quite know where to go. Is the point that man must evolve to go off world or evolve to find other planets upon which to live? were the 5th dimensionals aliens or future humans? Other parts of the story also didn't make much sense. For somebody that grew up when the space race was still 'a thing' I was hoping to see a story about mankind's resourcefulness and desire to explore. I wanted a film that showed the development of practical interstellar travel by present human ingenuity and the first such voyage to another star and the adventure that would ensue. Instead, in this future, it turns out that mankind has abandoned the desire to pursue science and engineering due to an environmental collapse and the politically-correct socialistic group-think types have taken over and believe that the moon landing was capitalist propaganda.wonderful. To top it off the instellar part is thanks to a deus ex machina wormhole that shows up with no apparent explanation - and nobody really cares to ask why. But here is the part of the film that ultimately sunk it in my eyes: So here we are (once again) with the typical American trope of a kid growing up resenting their parent because said parent promised them something that they ultimately failed to deliver. It doesn't matter that any reasonable person once becoming an adult would realize that the promise their parent made was completely beyond their ability to guarantee. It doesn't matter that this parent was knowingly risking life and limb on a mission that might save not only the future of the entire race but the child's own personal future as well - pretty much the definition of the word 'hero'. oh no. we have to be mad at daddy because he couldn't buy you a pony for christmas or whatever. The worst part is that after all that heartache he comes back decades in the future and gets laughed at by the medics because he thought they named the space station after him. Hello. The guy just traversed time and space. Back from a suicide mission. Decades in the future. He didn't age. And they treat him like he's some dumb no-nothing shmuck from the boonies. Seriously? To top it off he finally gets to see his now aged daughter...and she totally blows him off...and all of these descendants of his that are around her - have absolutely no reaction to the guy! Anyway, like the title states, it's competently made even if the story isn't quite there and it's still enjoyable such that i would recommend someone watch it, if they hadn't already seen it. The banter with the robots was enjoyable - in some ways they were the most interesting and most developed characters in the film.

history.title: Rick & Morty: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Great new series - I hope it lasts for a 10 seasons at least.
history.text: I'm not usually a fan of the stuff on adult swim...much of it seems to me like overly random trash for circle-jerking left-leaning gen-xers. Rick and Morty, however, is a welcome exception to all that. This show has just the right blend of quirky characters, sci-fi, off-color humor, and randomness that make it something more than the sum of its parts. It's kind of like a cross between the Simpsons and Futurama as re-imagined by George Carlin. Strongly recommended for sci-fi animation fans; but just remember, like much of adult(get it?) swim, it's obviously not for the kids - so don't give the show a bad rating because you can't figure out that this is NOT a children's show.

history.title: Falling Skies: Season 5 [Blu-ray]
history.text: I feel like I wasted my time with this series. Watching the final season became a chore predicated only on the fact that I had already invested so much time into it that I felt i had to see it to the end. There was also the blind hope that maybe - just maybe - the show might actually fulfill its potential. Unfortunately it never did. The depiction of resistance against alien invaders is simply a cartoon version of war. Too many tricks and gimmicks and plot twists that made no sense all the way up to the finale. There was a lot of filler and dead time (which is terrible considering these seasons had only about 10 episodes a piece). It's a shame because I did like Noah Wyle in his role....

history.review_title: Both a sci-fi show and a documentary but does not shine in either role
history.text: The intermix of sci-fi and documentary elements is a fairly jarring melange of styles. The documentary parts don't offer very much that a space enthusiast doesn't already know so I found myself skipping those after the first few episodes. The documentary portions suffer from the same superficial style and content that plagues most of the documentaries featured on the science popularizer channels like Discovery, Science, National Geographic etc. in that they don't really offer anything new or compelling to the space enthusiast. The drama portion has a few highlights but falls flat overall with some very dry main characters and a lot of talking heads in monotone narration. Hopefully they focus a bit more on the drama and less on the retread documentary aspect for season 2.

history.title: Brimstone [Blu-ray]
history.text: This film depicts violence and brutality to a level that goes beyond what is necessary to get any sort of larger point across; it seems more voyeuristic than anything else. From some online articles one gets the impression that the director and cast want this film to be seen as making a commentary on abuse against women and religious fundamentalism. I'm not sure what point they are trying to make. Do we really need to be shown the graphic flogging of a 5 year old girl after already having sat through numerous beatings, torturous killings, patricide, incestuous child abuse, tongues being cut and the murder of a child?

history.review_title: A mediocre Spacemonster movie with a twist ending that you can see from a mile away.
history.text: This is not a bad film, but it isn't an especially great one either. This is essentially an updated version of a 1950's 'monster from space' B-Movie ; one with modern A-grade effects work. Many have compared it to Alien which I suppose is valid but it doesn't provide the tension of that earlier film. Sadly there is nothing really unique here and even the 'twist' ending was easily intuited. Much of the plot is driven by character decisions and reactions that make no sense for a presumably highly trained crew entrusted with investigating the first known sample of extraterrestrial life. Examples include: There is no proper isolation of the organism. There is no emergency sterilization equipment for potentially infectious or hazardous organisms. Some characters at first care about quarantine and exposure and then alternately don't care about it. The ability to jettison such an organism out into space relies on a soyuz capsule that needs to be launched only after an emergency situation arises. Hopefully NASA and ESA are better than this in real life. All that said, if you just enjoy it as a popcorn monster movie then this film is can be enjoyable as a Saturday afternoon diversion.

history.title: It Came from Outer Space [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: A great film that is not given the treatment it deserves.
history.text: This is one of the best science fiction films of the 1950s for it's thoughtful take on a first contact situation that does not ultimately fall prey to the usual bug eyed monster tropes. This one ranks up there with 'This Island Earth' and 'Forbidden Planet' though it is not as widely known as those others (perhaps because it is in black and white?) That said the transfer of this film is near appalling. There is far to much graininess and noise in the transfer. There are times where the background shimmers almost like old tv static - i wouldn't be surprised if they simply used the DVD transfer for this.

history.review_title: Excellent film that's well worth watching. Scotty, beam me up.
history.text: Regarding the ending, I guess extremely over the top situations like those depicted in this movie really do happen; although it's not regular fare on the 10 o'clock news; thank God. That being said, these sort of characters really do exist, although I couldn't say with any certainty that the scenarios in this plot weren't intentionally over exaggerated to make the point; motel rooms completely covered in aluminum foil and that sort of thing, however, there indeed, undereducated, seriously drug addled junkies, war veterans with a host of mental issues and good for nothing, wife beating ex cons. These are three perfect ingredients for making a real killer cocktail. I could have easily given this 5 stars but something about the way in which the plot escalates doesn't strike me as being entirely plausible and is somewhat overacted towards the end. The film starts off well, very well, with bulls eye accurate character development; completely accurate and believable. Ashley Judd and Lynn Collins are superb, as is Michael Shannon. The initial appearance of the Michael Shannon character is well handled; the viewer's gut feeling is that something's not right here but is he a red herring or something more insidious? Overall this is an excellent movie but I feel it could have been handled with a little more finesse; not necessarily less dramatic because it couldn't possibly be otherwise, but not being a film director, I just can't put my finger on it.

history.title: Woman in Black
history.review_title: This is still the best version that evokes true psychological terror.
history.text: This is still the best cinematic version of the Susan Hill story which was undoubtedly the inspiration for the plot of the Ethan Hawke movie "Sinister" which is also excellent; terrifying in fact. I'm impressed by the way eel marsh house must have been inspired by the French Island of Mont Saint-Michel, which in olden days was also accessible only by a muddy causeway and subject to the treacherous nature of the tides. Although this is a low budget film, it still succeeds by leaps and bounds over the 2012 Daniel Radcliffe/Ciarán Hinds production, which is rife with unnecessary and overused contrivances, particularly the depiction of Mrs. Daly who "channels" the spirit of her dead son and the scene wherein the body of the dead boy is pulled out of the mud in an attempt to finally put his soul at rest. The advantages of modern technology to provide a convincing atmosphere of gloom and horror are wasted and mired in the plots predictable manner of depicting the tragedies wrought by the vengeful spirits and the attempts to placate them; it's as if the script was taken from passages of "How to Deal With Evil Spirits 101". This earlier version treats the Susan Hill novella as the author herself might have intended, by focusing on the most vital aspects of the storyline with only minor embellishments. One of the most frightening scenes is that of the evil spirit manifesting herself on the surface of the lake where Kipps' family is drowned. In this scene we see her only at a distance, but the visual effect is riveting; very similar to the scene in "The Innocents" (Deborah Kerr) wherein the dead governess appears in the very distant clump of marsh reeds. This technique straddles the emotional boundaries of what is implied and what is depicted which very effectively provides the stimuli to evoke a true sense of menace and horror. Although there are other deceptively simple techniques sprinkled throughout the film, they provide maximum effect in creating a profoundly horrific psychological effect.

history.title: The Cell (2000)
history.review_title: This is a magnificent film of rare quality and achievement.
history.text: This is the latest and most successful cinematic attempt at elucidating the ideas about using scientific technology to explore and directly access the human conscienceness and enter the realm of the human psyche. Predecessors of the "The Cell" include "Altered States" with William Hurt, "Flatliners" starring Kiefer Sutherland and "Brainstorm" starring Chrstopher Walken.; all of which are excellent films, each in their own right. I suggest that all three films should be viewed prior to watching "The Cell" in order to gain a better understanding of how these concepts have evolved and are brilliantly brought to fruition in this film. Jennifer Lopez shines as a Madonna-like character in this visually breathtaking amalgam of the three concepts touched upon by the aforementioned films, which offer glimpses into different, although not necessarily divergent aspects of the theoretical possibility of linking the intellectual and spiritual aspects of humanity through direct manipulation of the human condition in it's various aspects. "The Cell" also succeeds in evoking a profound emotional response; and perhaps even an unexpected spiritual awakening in the viewer. The artistic conceptualization and cinematography are exquisitely sublime, and the characterizations of the various players are nothing short of genius. The supporting cast is not merely "supportive" in the conventional sense but are as vitally intrinsic to the plot as the key actors themselves. This is a rare feat and is as impressive as are the sets and costumes which are not only spellbinding but are also as convincingly pertinent to the storyline as the actors themselves; not to be viewed as mere props and backdrops. "The Cell" is no mere exercise in visual mesmerization for it's own sake; this film compels the viewer without his/her own consent to undergo a self examination of ones own spirituality and belief systems.

history.title: The Haunting
history.review_title: An unmitigated disaster, that's the only scary element of this remake.
history.text: My only and favorite scene is Theo describing her attire: Eleanor " Nell" Vance: I love your boots. Theo: Oh, you do? Thanks! Prada; Milan, not New York. The rest of the movie is just an unrelenting series of CG special effects, most of which are ridiculous and altogether destroys any sense of the psychological horror element that defines the spirit of the original story. The true nature of the characters have been mangled beyond recognition and the overall plot is likewise massacred. This latest version of the much beloved Susan Hill horror classic is nothing more than a ham handed, insensitive re-write of the original source material; nothing more than a poor excuse for a deafening cacophony of senseless digitized effects. Dr. Markway's premise that this is a study of insomniacs is pointless and rife with silly frames of Luke popping sleeping pills out of a Pez dispenser and other clumsy absurdities. This is nothing more than a study in using computer technology to compensate for a terrible script and taking artistic liberties with disastrous consequences. The only version worth watching is the earlier and iconic 1963 film with Claire Bloom and Julie Harris.

history.review_title: Amazon productions has outdone itself. "The Collection" is an unequivocal and monumental triumph.
history.text: So far, one of the best Amazon productions ever conceived. This is entertainment that not only delights the eye but inspires the viewer to think and investigate, which in this case is a necessity if one is to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the circumstances upon which this story is set. For instance, how many "Star Trek" fans would know that the the term "Maquis" and their activities was not a mere flight of fancy, but one of the names attributed to the French Resistance. Do your homework. This is heady material, accusations of Nazi collusion, rapacious schemes of treachery and double dealings, blackmail, murder and not least of all; a true behind the scenes insight into the nitty gritty realities and not always so pretty world of the fashion industry. The writing and cinematography are first rate and the success of these online productions suggest that perhaps the monopoly of the "big screen" approach to cinematic entertainment is beginning to show a few cracks. For the sake of brevity, it's almost impossible to provide comprehensive descriptions of this colorful cast of characters who are as complex as the circumstances in which they play out their roles in this provocative and gut grinding production. The idiosyncratic elements of levity are sparse but not frivolous; they are in perfect synch with the attributes of each character and their extenuating circumstances; all of which are as complex as the efforts that went into creating the breathtaking sartorial confections. This production is a work of genius because the grim state of post WWII Europe provides what is possibly the perfect backdrop for a storyline of this magnitude; it is an understatement to say that this is possibly the most fertile ground in which the relevancies of this story could flourish and display the entire range of humanities strengths and failings and the consequences that ensue. I am hoping for a second season as there are far too many unanswered questions and possible outcomes; this is not a trite cliff hanger from a conventional televised soap opera. As far as unanswered questions and loose threads (pardon the pun) go, I would venture to guess that Frederic Lemaire, who was once Sabine's employer and mentor; and who is ruthlessly coerced and maneuvered into retirement by Paul sabine; had much to do with the published implication of Sabine as a collaborator. The House of Lemaire is an old and established name in French couture, and although Sabine claims that it's time for the "old" to step down and make way for the "new"; Lemaire cautions him by reminding Sabine that he, Lemaire, has a medal of honor from De Gaulle; what does Sabine have? One must recall that Lemaire was cleverly using Sabine as a negotiator between Paris, Berlin and Austria in a bid to keep Paris as the fashion capitol of the world; Sabine was doing the dirty work for Lemaire who kept himself in the shadows and out of the spotlight of scrutiny. It's only logical that Lemaire was merely "returning the favor" in his feud with Paul Sabine; hence the persistence of the reporter Rossi whose efforts culminate in a damning accusation of collaboration on the part of Paul Sabine in the French newspapers. As a seamstress at the House of Sabine remarks, (paraphrased) if a German soldier offered her a seat on a bus, would she remain standing or take the seat? An interesting dilemma as she concludes that people back then and now, are "quick to judge". Guilt by overt action or even a presumably "innocent" association is still perceived as guilt, no matter what the circumstances may be.

history.review_title: This is a rare and outstanding HBO production that is an indisputable triumph for Tom Stoppard and viewers alike.
history.text: Out of all the period dramas ever produced, this HBO miniseries evokes the splendor of a magnificent parure of jewels. "Parade's End" vies for the limelight with many of it's contemporaries, but all too often they are only pieces of the full set. I have only watched the first episode and I can instantly tell that this is a winner, hands down. It's like a really good book; you only have to read the first couple of pages to know that the writing is first rate; and so it is with "Parade's End". This takes the cinematic tradition of the much lauded "Merchant, Ivory" films to a new level, and the inimitable Tom Stoppard is the man to do it. Although the draw of Mr. Cumberbatch as one of the principle and more recognizable names in not without merit, his fellow actors are equally gifted and compliment each other's performances in their respective roles to perfection; this is nothing less than an assemblage of brilliantly casted actors. The production values are sumptuous, yet appropriately so and the dialogue is written and delivered with unflinching vigor and graceful subtlety. The cinematography and editing are executed with breathtaking deftness and reveals the mastery of a gifted eye that treats the viewer to an eloquent film crafted with remarkable aplomb.
