To think that somebody could waste their time and energy in making a movie like this is amazing. I would describe the 2 parents as anti-social sociopaths not artists. Utter waste of my time.

history.title: Far From the Madding Crowd
history.review_title: Why ----- would anyone want to do a remake of the most beautiful PERFECT MOVIE
history.text: SERIOUSLY. How could anyone possibly top the original? No way. You are wasting your time and money. No one will ever top the original.

history.title: The Lady In The Van
history.text: POSSIBLE SPOILERS: I see myself in the same position in a few years. Not by choice. It is true that "going downhill is an uphill job". With that --- this movie is charming and delightful even though the reality of the situation is very real and very sad. But not sad when you realize that you accept the reality that you are now living in ----- a van. It's main impact on me is that someone --- who would probably never consider doing what he did --- let her park her van in his driveway for a few months ---- that lasted 15 years!!!!! The thing is: I understand her plight. No home, no family, no place to live -- except in her van and hopefully in a safe area. That's all she really wants. Living homeless and in a van is a lifestyle--- when you really can't afford anything else. She kept her sense of self, her dignity, self integrity, and an extremely strong will to survive. This is based on a true story. Kudos to the man who helped her. Last but not least ---- it has given me tips on how to live homeless and survive.

history.review_title: I wish I had my 45 minutes back.
history.text: Gave this a chance. I found it really really boring. Stopped watching after 45 minutes as it was unbearable. I'm wondering if people were paid to give this a 5 Star review?

POSSIBLE SPOILER: This is a great movie! I did not know what to expect having not read any reviews or synopsis. It seems that every time I'm flipping the channels and this is on cable, I can't stop myself from watching. If you have ever watched or experienced a bully or being bullied ----- this is the ultimate "Get back".

history.review_title: WAITING FOR SOMETHING TO HAPPEN WHILE WATCHING PAINT DRY.
history.text: The acting is good but the movie itself is slightly better than watching paint dry. Ever so slightly. Waiting for something to happen. The ending --- a big disappointment. Putting myself in her shoes ---- I get it.

history.title: Cold Comes the Night
history.text: I expected this to be a just another low budget, boring, poorly acted movie. It definitely held my interest for the duration of the movie.
The thought of something like this happening is gruesome to say the least. Hang in there. Gotta give it a rating of 5 for the unexpected twists and turns.

history.review_title: THRILLER !!! GREAT MOVIE ! YOU WON'T BE DISAPPOINTED !!!!!
history.text: I love this movie. I'll watch any movie with Billy Bob Thornton as I am never disappointed. Pretty much same for Bill Paxton. Billy Bob is plain and simple an Oscar winning actor. I have a hard time with movies that take a long time to "get off the ground". This one took about 5 minutes and I couldn't stop watching it. Lots of morals to be learned from this story. Still can't figure out the "pine apple" joke. James Coburn won the Oscar that year for the movie "Affliction" which he well deserved. The Academy should have called a tie and given Billy Bob Thornton one also. He was SO GOOD in this movie !!!!!!! ( I wonder if his hairstylist won any awards😉 )

history.review_title: DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND WATCH THIS MOVIE !!! Surprisingly HILARIOUS !!!!!!!
history.text: I would have never watched this movie as I thought it would just be stupid ---- but I stumbled on it as I was flipping the channels and ended up watching it. It is so hilarious !!!!! I've watched it numerous times and crack up just as if I'm watching it for the first time. Will Anett's facial expressions are priceless. You just know what he is thinking when "Barry is making the move". It truly is one of my favorites.

history.title: The Wizard of Lies
history.review_title: I THOUGHT I HEARD ENOUGH ABOUT BERNIE MADOFF --- but
history.text: For me, once I started watching this I could not stop. Robert DeNiro IS Bernie Madoff---- but then --- so was Richard Dreyfous. They were both great. Richard Dreyfous' portrayal -- I was convinced he was Madoff. Robert DeNiro --- convinced in a different way. Maybe Richard Dreyfous being Jewish had a leg up on DeNiro. Michelle Pfeiffer was the PERFECT RUTH MADOFF --- in style, speech, demeanor, looks, hair style, her face, her lips, her clothes, her inflections ----- Michelle Pfeiffer NAILED THE PART OF RUTH MADDOFF. This movie felt like it took you right there with all the characters involved. It is definitely worth the watch !

history.title: Apocalypto [Import belge]
history.review_title: IT's ONE OF THOSE MOVIES THAT ONCE YOU START WATCHING --- YOU CAN'T STOP !!!!!!
history.text: This movie is incredibly fantastic. I felt like I was there living there through the entire movie ---- on the edge of my seat. The scenery is gorgeous, the acting superb. Everything about this movie is 5 STARS. This definitely deserved BEST MOVIE OSCAR and a whole slew of other Oscars. After watching this ---- I realized that Mel Gibson is a genius.

history.review_title: Spoiler Alert !!! I would highly recommend this movie
history.text: Spoiler Alert !!!!!!First time I started watching this, I thought it was a great movie until ----- the turn of events that I found so depressing. Elizabeth Taylor, of course, beautiful and upbeat. Montgomery Clift --- well ----- I could watch him on the screen if he was just staring into the camera for 3 hours. ---- and Shelley Winters --- so morose, dull and downtrodden. She played that part to a perfection. Put yourself in George's shoes (Montgomery Clift) ----- a message for us all ---- but how could he have foreseen the future. What a life he could have had if he had not used poor judgement. That one initial decision ruined his life. You never know what can come into your life in an instant changing it for the better ----- or the worse. As depressing as it is I would highly recommend this movie. I can't help myself from watching it periodically. ----- hoping for a different ending.

history.review_title: THIS IS AN UNDERATED COOL MOVIE !! THERE NEEDS TO BE A SEQUEL.
history.text: I thought this was going to be a stupid B movie. It's not. It really held my interest. Movie starts off with a real twist rather than ending with one. "I admit --- I did not see that coming" . Luke Evans is a very good actor. And if this was one of the worst movies ---- he is great to look at. He reminds me of a very good looking Leonardo DiCaprio. All of the cast acted well. Great ending soundtrack that is perfectly in sync with the scene.

history.review_title: I WOULD GIVE THIS A ZERO IF I COULD !!!!!
history.text: Simply ---- this is the worst movie that I've ever seen. It is so depressing and boring with zero substance. Not the least bit entertaining. A total waste of my time. Totally stupid.

history.title: The Best of Everything
history.review_title: Worth the watch if just to see Suzy Parker in that RED DRESS.
history.text: I leaned ALOT from this movie. I was a very young 12 yr old when I first saw it --- but it had a lasting impression on me. I guess the most important thing I learned from this movie was to not be naive and let any guy take advantage of me ---because grief and personal regret was right around the corner. I stuck to that philosophy and it served me well. I love looking at the street scenes of New York City from the late '50s. All the women were beautiful --- especially Suzy Parker ---- and oh that RED DRESS. You don't see that kind of class and good taste any more. The plot of the movie is not rocket science but a simple enjoyable story with a simple but worthwhile message.

history.title: Good Ol' Freda
history.review_title: IF YOU LIVED THROUGH AND LOVED THE BEATLES IN THE '60s, YOU ARE GOING TO LOVE THIS FILM !
history.text: Yep. This took me on a wonderful trip down memory lane. It is very hard to describe the feelings experienced at that time in the early '60s. Anything wonderful was possible. The Beatles were so different than anything we had before. It was a thrilling time to be around. Freda Kelley had the job to die for being a part of this wonderful world phenomena. It was hard to even blink while watching the film for fear of missing ANYTHING. Highly recommend it.

history.title: The Boy (2016)
history.review_title: IF YOU ENJOY WATCHING PAINT DRY --- YOU WILL LOVE THIS MOVIE.
history.text: I should have done with this movie what I do with programs on the ID channel. Watch the first 7 minutes (if it remotely holds my interest) and then the last 3. Saves me 50 minutes.

history.review_title: IT IS A LITTLE HARD TO WATCH BUT IT WILL HOLD YOUR INTEREST.
history.text: Rebecca de Morney played the "matriarch" to a tee. Very good acting on her part. The movie did hold my interest till the end.

history.title: Hell Or High Water
history.review_title: WATCHING PAINT DRY IS MUCH MORE HIGHLY ENTERTAINING !!
history.text: I'm into this right now for over a tortuous hour. "What about Bob" is coming on now on another channel. I have no choice. I'd rather watch Bob Wiley for the 45th time than sit through this for another 60 seconds. ---- and is Jeff Bridges ever going to talk normal again without that old man raspy voice? Are we ever going to see the handsome Jeff Bridges again or is it always going to be this long hair, bearded, scraggly, (the have not shaved in over a week) dirty looking guy as of years late? I mean --- can't he scrub up for at least one more decent movie? Anyway, this is one boring ass movie. Can't possibly imagine why anyone would give it more than one star. And even THAT is a stretch.

history.title: The Band Wagon (Two-Disc Special Edition)
history.review_title: So very much to enjoy...a Christmas pudding, but, beware...
history.text: "The Band Wagon" cannot be loved as can "Singing in the Rain". It is not as picturesquely beautiful as "Gigi". It lacks the bawdy good humour of "Seven Brides for Seven Brothers". But it is the best musical ever made. For those who do not appreciate it, go put on your "Saturday Night Fever" or "Xanadu" because you're simply from the wrong age. But this reissue carries a plague with it. The narration for "Singing in the Rain" added to the movie, so one was added here, too. Please, don't listen to it; if you love musicals, don't listen to it. If you like music, don't listen to it. It is atrocious and should be stripped away as soon as possible. Michael Feinstein is a good singer, but he grovels at Liza Minelli's feet here and sounds like a total loss. And what connection does he have with the movie? None. He really can add nothing but stumble his way through the "I love Liza" illness that he suffers from. And Minelli? Take her away. She is so concerned about her life and "Mama" that she makes you want to gag. Hey, Liza, Judy wasn't in this movie, so enough already. And her 'insights' are stupid and contribute nothing to our knowledge of this gorgeous film. Drivel is drivel, no matter the source. The other extra are all right, but nothing to get excited about. Now, the snippets of footage from the cut songs, "Two Faced Woman" is the only one dealt with in this set, would have been great to have, regardless of the quality. So, buy it for the film. This is a beautiful print and the sound has never been better balanced. 'High and Low' emerges tenderley as the introduction to 'Dancing in the Dark' which has to be the most beautiful piece of dance ever committed to film. I've had my copy for years, play it often. You can't grow tired of it, unless you're a Morlock.

history.title: Billy Rose's Jumbo
history.review_title: They just don't make 'em like this anymore
history.text: One of Doris Day's best musicals - nothing can touch "Love Me or Leave Me" - plus Martha Raye and Jimmy Durante. And Stephen Boyd for the ladies. The songs are fabulous Rogers and Hart at their best. The only thing missing is a proper ending. The last number is fun, but it doesn't solve the plot problems. Yes, Day gets Boyd, Raye has Durante, but what about the circus, the point of the whole movie? Limbo....

history.title: Silk Stockings
history.review_title: The last of the big MGM musicals...They almost got it right.
history.text: MGM's production of "Silk Stockings" was vastly superior to the second rate Cole Porter Broadway musical on which it was based, to a great extent because the leading lady, Hildegarde Neff, could neither sing nor dance. Of course, Charisse is dubbed, as she always was, though her very infrequent stage appearances proved that the voice was on key, but too faint unless she was miked heavily. But the lady could sure dance. 'Dancing in the Dark' in :"The Bandwagon" also with Astaire, and the best musical ever made, is the most romantic moment on film, bar none. But the title song, as danced here by Charisse is as beautiful a number as she has ever filmed. (I have to block out 'One Alone' from "Deep in My Heart" as James Mitchell, finally given a chance to dance in an MGM musical, actually steals the number from her no matter how good she is.) Janis Paige is a hoot as a 'dumb' Esther Williams - Williams was not dumb. But Paige is great. And who would have thought that Peter Lorre would make such a good comedian? Astaire and Charisse are perfection together - they always were. But Astaire's final solo should have been dumped before filming. It is the only clunker in the movie's score - the worst of the Broadway show was long gone. He does what he can with it, but it is a losing cause as the song, 'The Ritz Rock and Roll' was dated when it was filmed and has become a pathetic piece of film now. Otherwise, they are magic- but not 'Dancing in the Dark' magic, which surpassed anything Astaire performed with any of his other leading ladies. Yes, including Ginger. For fun, watch Charisse's skirt become a skort, and then a skirt and then.....with really no reason except that the censor board must have hovered over the set making sure that neither the title song nor Paige's 'Silk and Satin' went beyond their limited line. They both did. Never underestimate Arthur Freed when he was determined to get around them. So if this is not in your collection, add it. You won't regret it, though you may fastforward it through the 'Ritz".

history.title: Cover Girl
history.text: "Cover Girl" is a film that almost never was made. Hayworth had made two films with Astaire that she treasured. He was not available and the part was then to be cast with a non-dancer. That didn't balance the film. MGM said 'no' to loaning out Gene Kelly and offered another dancer who was considered too young for Hayworth. Back to the drawing boards. But Kelly began to push LBM and got his way as long as he agreed to two films that MGM wanted him to make, one a nonmusical. Now, the technical aspects started to get in the way. Columbia wanted colour. Columbia could get it, but it meant time and money, neither of which Columbia liked to lose. Convenient illnesses held up the start of production. Then the stars were in alignment, and the movie began, though costumes were still a problem. Looking for something 'different', they finally decided upon ridiculous hats, which Hayworth refused to wear, but Eve Arden looked fabulous in them. And shooting began. Then it stopped while everyone tried to figure out just how to film the solo that Gene Kelly wanted to do, knew how to do, told them how to do, and drew a few days of blank stares. And from that point on, all went smoothly. Musicals should all have such problems if the results are to be this good. What is here is hard to criticize unless one gets truly petty - like how big a stage would a Broadway theatre have to have in order to stage the title number? Yep, Madison Square Garden size, doubled. But it is so gorgeous that one tosses aside logic and lets it wash over you. What is Gloria DeHaven doing in this film when she had already signed with MGM and had far bigger roles? And here, is she even billed? But to heck with all that. Sit back and enjoy one of the few great musicals that MGM did not produce, and in Wartime, too. Just remember, without Hayworth, gloriously talented Hayworth (Watch her in "Separate Tables" to see the full range of that talent) this film would never, problems or not, have been made. If you don't own it - and this is my second CD of the film - buy it now. You'll have to hate musicals not to fall in love with this one.

history.title: Halt and Catch Fire: Season 1 [Blu-ray]
history.text: "Halt and Catch Fire" is so well done that you almost believe it is factual. Part of that is due to the cast, especially Lee Pace who has to walk a fine line between being a louse and a decent human being; and he pulls it off. The insecurities of the character are the giveaways of the real personality and the driving force of this series. Against the lies told, more for his own necessary illusions about himself, they inform us of the other characters true natures. One, Mackenzie Davis, believes only what she chooses, and her choices are usually right, but occasionally spectacularly wrong.This makes her role another difficult one to grasp. The third main character, Scoot McNairy as Joe, is so wrapped up in his work and fears that he sees little as it is, but acts as the anchor that holds it all together. Like real people, it takes a long haul to really get to know them, and even longer to understand them. Be patient; it is worth it. Also, don't watch this series just for amusement; keep your mind alert for all the subtle machiavellian moves. Don't fear the technical side. Most of it is plausible, but unnecessary to the characters - it is the highway that allows us to travel with them and learn a good deal about them and the early years of computer research. All in all, a series that is caviar. It will take about three episodes to grab you, but then it will not let go. Technically, of course, this is a well written, acted, shot piece of the drama of life, with just enough humour to keep us going.

history.title: Les Girls [DVD]
history.review_title: Wait for TCM to show it.
history.text: "Les Girls" might have been a great musical if it had been made ten years earlier. Quite clearly, MGM was no longer willing to spend the money and the time on musicals any longer. The photography is sloppy, as it is in "It's Always Fair Weather", lacking the sharpness and intelligent use of angles and keeping clutter from the dancers' feet. And what could have possessed Mitzi Gaynor to take a role in a film where she doesn't get to sing a solo and her one major number is as a foil for Gene Kelly? Perhaps she should have had a good talk with Cyd Charisse who commented that dancing with Astaire was heaven, with Kelly, hell. The Cole Porter score is functional but there is nothing there to whistle or hum to, and most must have been remnants from his trunk full of discarded songs, what few there are. And the book - oh, where does one start with that mess? With a few good writers, a lot of care, and ruthless rewriting, it might have worked. But it is a slap-dash affair, unworthy to be compared with any of the MGM magical musical of the past. "Lili", for instance, had few songs, but one smash hit, and was presented with such style and charm that it became one of the first MGM musicals to be transferred to Broadway. Buy this if you are a Gaynor fan. Buy it if you loved Kay Kendall, but don't expect her to have much to do of value in this script. Buy this if you want to see an opening number that is so over the top that ego trumps skill every second the song goes on, and on, and on.

history.title: Man of Steel (Blu-ray)
history.review_title: How to turn an actor into a buffoon.
history.text: Poor Henry Cavill. He had a great career going and then he took on the part of Superman. It made him look like 'this year's pumped up talentless oaf". And he hasn't had a truly good role since. Head back to England, Henry, before Hollywood turns you into a joke. The script, as so much of the Superman and Batman movies, is atrociously badly written, though I am certain that the grade one students who wrote it had fun, none of which the movie goers had.Perhaps he needs a new and much better agent as anyone who encouraged him to do this and the sequels, must have been money mad and totally insane. Consider it as a version of the plague and stay away.

history.title: Oblivion [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The title says it all. Send the film into oblivion, and any idea of a sequel....arghhhhh.
history.text: I bought this over a year ago, played it once and tried to give it away. No one wanted it. I have not played it since. It is, to put it mildly, a bad movie. Universal has a habit of turning out dreadful films headed by a 'star' in which they are hoping to cash in on his name and care not about the quality of the film. Then, just to keep us off guard, they actually make a super film; this is not one of those super films. Cruise has become a joke version of himself and only with an especially well written film has he got a chance. At the moment I am waiting for him to make a film with Charlize Theron in which she will literally mop the floor with him and mercilessly put him out of his misery. No, Tom, you are not Ron Hubbard; you are not even Tom Cruise any more.

history.review_title: Now if the series were only on D VD.
history.text: So much better than the earlier De Niro film. This one explores Stahr faster and with more depth...though the hand to the heart comes too soon - Norman Shearer isn't even around yet. But the sets, the costumes, the music are all spot on. And as to the cast- perfection. .

history.title: John Wick: Chapter 2 [Blu-ray+DVD+ Digital HD]
history.text: Better, most of the time, than the original. And you can't say that about most sequels.

history.title: Logan
history.review_title: Fast forward a few sce nes and it's perfect!
history.text: I would give this one five stars, but too many scenes are allowed to go on too long. Also, I wish Hugh Jackman had not made it so soon after his surgery; it gets a little eerie at times when it shouldn't. But it is one of his best performances and a fitting end to the cycle.

history.title: Kiss Me, Kate [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: Where's Ann MIller when you need her?
history.text: Rachel York and the actress playing Bianca are the weak links here. Brent Barrett's 'Fred' ranks with the best, and, as almost always the case. Also, "Bianca" the song Porter wrote knowing it would be cut, but Harold Lang's contract demanded a solo in Act Two, and Lang made this one of the standouts of the original show. And so it is here. MGM did it better, but tinkered with it a lot- and thank heaven - since it gace us one of the best dabnce numbers in "From This Moment On", a otal throwaway here.

history.title: Without Warning (Bluray/DVD Combo) [Blu-ray]
history.text: Loved this movie. I remember when it was first released. I was young and though it was a little scary and when I saw it on DVD I just had to have it for my collection. Now it seems a little cheesy, but I enjoyed just as much as I did the first time I saw it. A great addition to my collection.

history.title: Wonder Woman: Season 3
history.text: Wonder Woman was one of my favorite shows back in the 70's and when I saw that I could get them all on DVD I jumped at the chance. This is a great series with good storylines and good morals to teach. They sure don't make them like this anymore.

history.title: The Six Million Dollar Man: Season 1
history.review_title: Six Million Dollar Man, a great show.
history.text: Another of my favorite t.v. shows. This season was just as good as I remembered. Love it.

history.title: Annabelle (DVD)
history.text: This movie was very disappointing. There was a lot of hype about this movie that had it built up to be one of the scariest movies of all time. Very disappointed. The scariest part of this movie was when the crazy woman rushed into the house and stabbed the woman.

history.title: The Crater Lake Monster [DVD]
history.text: I loved this movie. These old 70's movies are somewhat cheesy by today's standards, but I still enjoy watching them. Anyone that likes creature features this will be a great addition to their collection and one worth watching.

history.title: Paranormal Case Files: Ghost Investigations
history.text: This DVD was not what I thought it would be. I love watching the Ghost Hunters, Ghost Adventures and Paranormal Witness but I was a bit disappointed in this DVD.

history.title: The Bionic Woman: Season 3
history.text: The Bionic Woman was another show I enjoyed back in the 70's. I especially liked the episodes with the bionic dog. Great show and this season was just as good as I remember. Loved it.

history.title: Starsky & Hutch The Complete Series
history.text: This was wonderful. I was a huge fan of Starsky and Hutch back in the 70"s. It was one of my favorite t.v. shows. I have already been through two of the seasons and the episodes are just as I remembered them. I love this item. I would recommend this to any Starsky and Hutch fan.

history.title: The Six Million Dollar Man: Season 4
history.text: The Six Million Dollar Man was another one of my favorite T.V. programs from the 70's. I was in love with Col. Steve Austin. He was every girl's dream man. These episodes were wonderful and were just as I remembered them. Some episodes I had forgotten about but they were awesome. One of my favorite episodes were A Bionic Christmas Carol. Steve dressed as Santa and posed as the ghosts of Christmas in order to help a man change his ways so he would help his nephew and family. This is a great buy and I would recommend it to any Six Million Dollar Man fans.

history.title: WWE: Bret "Hitman" Hart - The Best There Is, The Best There Was, The Best There Ever Will Be
history.text: This was actually purchased as a gift for my brother. When he opened the package he was surprised. He was a huge fan of Bret hart and he collects his memorabilia. He was very pleased with the gift.

history.title: Night of the Demons [DVD]
history.text: This is one wicked movie. I enjoyed this movie and it made a great addition to my horror collection. Great buy. Would recommend it to all horror fans.

history.title: Night of the Demons 2 [DVD]
history.text: Another great installment of the Demons franchise. A very sinister movie and another great choice for horror fans. A good movie to play for your Halloween fright night fest.

history.title: Porky's the Ultimate Collection
history.text: I have never been a fan of comedies. For the most part I loath most comedies. I don't find them funny instead I find them ridiculously stupid. Porky's is the exception to that rule. Porky's is extremely funny and as close to being just like what might happen with high school kids as you can get. I loved these movies. This is a must for any comedy fan's library.

history.title: Partners In Hell
history.text: This is another one of those comedies that is an exception to my comedy rule. Trinity and Bambino are the best. You've just got to love their humor, their abilities (in the movie) and their bumbling, unwitting knack for doing the right thing. These two guys are outlaws, but are probably the worst outlaws of all time. This movie is a treasure and a must for anyone that loves good comedy.

history.title: 13th Child: Legend Of The Jersey Devil
history.text: I was a little disappointed in this DVD. When I purchased it I was under the impression that it was a movie, but it was a documentary telling the story of the Jersey Devil. It was an interesting story and my son was somewhat intrigued, but both of us was hoping for a movie. Anyone curious about and interested in the paranormal or cryptozoology will love this DVD. I do recommend this to anyone interested in cryptids.

history.title: Morris Costumes Hanging Phantom 72 In Animated
history.text: Love this product. This hanging phantom made a very nice addition to my haunted trail. The phantom in combination with a blue strobe light was very effective. I would recommend this to others.

history.title: The Good Witch Collection (The Good Witch's Garden / Good Witch's Gift / The Good Witch's Family / The Good Witch's Charm) (Hallmark)
history.text: The Good Witch Collection is one of the best movie series that I have seen in a long time. From the first time I saw the first installment "The Good Witch", I was hooked. Love these movies and recommend them to anyone that loves mystery and intrigue.

history.title: Night of the Lepus
history.text: Great movie. My son calls it cheesy, but he don't have the appreciation for great classic horror films. I saw this for the first time back in the 70's on the late show. Back then it was a little scary, but now it's a little comical. I still love this movie. It is what I grew up watching. I recommend it to anyone that likes the old horror movies.

history.title: Sci-Fi Creature Classics - 4-Movie Set - 20 Million Miles to Earth - The Giant Claw - It Came From Beneath The Sea - Mothra
history.text: Talk about your cheesy movies. I love these movies. I actually bought this DVD because of the "Giant Claw" but the others was a pleasant extra. Today's generation don't have the appreciation for those old movies, but I find them entertaining. Great find.

history.title: Stephen King's It (Double Sided Disc)
history.text: This is an awesome movie. The third copy I have bought. My son absolutely loves it. Pennywise is the creepiest clown I have ever seen and he's what got my sister afraid of clowns. Scary, creepy movie.

history.text: I enjoyed watching Oprah in this production of the book I read decades ago!

history.title: You Got To Move - Stories Of Change In The South
history.text: I saw this program on the television months ago. It was so inspiring that I bought it to be able to share these stories with my daughter and my grandchildren.

history.title: Fences [DVD]
history.text: This is a fabulous rendition of August Wilson's play, due to the writing of the playwrite, August Wilson, and the wonderful cast. Denzel Washington should have won the best male acting Oscar. I bought this DVD because the movie was too long to sit through with the 40 minutes of awful commercials that movie goers have to go through to see films nowadays. It was well worth the price of the DVD.

history.title: Nina
history.text: I understand why the surviving family of Nina Simone may have objected to this portrayal of the fabulously talented, but troubled Nia Simone. In all fairness to the the actress, I cannot think of a single actress or singer today who could portray Nina Simone. Nina Simone's voice was too distinctive for anyone to copy, and her piano playing was also too passionate for anyone other than a great pianist to imitate her style. The movie was unsatisfying in leaving out large gaps of Nina Simone's life. However, the actor David Oyelowo, did a wonderful job playing the supportive friend and eventual manager of Nina Simone, in spite of the ordeals he faced dealing with his friend's difficult behavior and mental illness.

history.title: Manchester By The Sea
history.text: I am shocked that Casey Affleck won the best actor Oscar this year, now that I have seen the movie. I ordered this DVD because I was curious about the story but the movie was too long to watch in a theater. I am thankful I did not have to sit through this 2 hour plus film. I disliked the two main male characters too much to care what happened to either of them by the end of the movie. I feel for Michelle Williams, who was excellent in the role of the ex-wife, as her acting talent seems to go unrewarded year after year.

history.title: Dirty Rotten Scoundrels (RPKG/DVD)
history.text: I saw this movie years ago, but I ordered it to have a copy available for friends who might have missed it in the theaters.

history.title: Scrooged
history.text: This is a family favorite take-off on one of my favorite classic Christmas tales, A Christmas Carol. Bill Murray is at his best, and the rest of the cast is fabulous as well.

history.title: Doctor Zhivago (Deluxe Edition)
history.text: This is one of my all-time favorite films. I wanted to have the movie on-hand for my grandchildren.

history.title: Jason Bourne
history.text: I like Matt Damon as Jason Bourne, but this episode is so violent I had to hid my eyes every other scene. Therefore, I lost track of the story several times. The viewer needs to be able to watch a lot of violence. I can't.

history.title: 12 YEARS A SLAVE (DVD/WS-2.40/ENG SDH-SP SUB) 12 YEARS A SLAVE (DVD/WS-2.40/ENG
history.review_title: Great movie about a shameful history
history.text: This is a wonderfully acted movie of a shameful part of American history. It is difficult to watch people trapped into slavery, and the violence they are subjected to on southern plantations, long after the Emancipation Proclamation suppoedly set them "free". It is a very sad story, but well-paced, with a fabulous cast. It was shocking to see actors I respect in other movies play the role of villains so convincingly in this tragic tale of man's inhumanity to his fellow man. Thankfully, the protagonist eventually regains his freedom, but after suffering terrible personal losses.

history.title: Moonlight
history.review_title: I was surprised how much I enjoyed this film
history.text: I was surprised how much I enjoyed this film, mainly because of the wonderful cast, and the fact that the story was very well paced. I was afraid the story around drug addiction might include a lot of violence, but the scenes of drugs were not too graphic. This is a must-see film, in my opinion, when government funds for schools and out-reach programs threaten to be cut.

history.title: Rick Steves' France DVD & Blu-Ray 20002014
history.text: This is the best travel guide through Paris, and other parts of France, that I know of. My late husband was French, and we traveled to Paris regularly to visit my in-laws for about twenty years. I no longer travel in Europe, so I treasure the images of the sights in Paris, and the rest of France. It might be a nice gift for first-time visitors to France.

history.title: Too Far to Go
history.review_title: Beautifully acted story of the end of a marriage
history.text: I bought this DVD because I had seen only the end of one episode on television years ago. I think it is one of the best programs ever on a marrigae falling apart, especially with the fabulous actress, Blythe Danner in the role of the wife! I was not used to seeing Michael Moriarty in the role of a "jerk" but he played the role of a bad husband exceptionally well. It's a sad, but beautifully acted and scripted production.

history.title: We Were the Mulvaneys
history.review_title: Sad, but beautiful story of a family's "fall from grace"
history.text: I loved this book by Joyce Carol Oates, and this production is every bit as good as the book! history.title: The Cutting Edge
history.text: Love this film ! (Not very many Blu-ray reviews to be found yet, so here's some insight) .....Great film, however, the current Blu-ray release has very poor picture quality. Let me explain. The first 15 minutes of the film is especially poor with heavy grain and what looks like smoke or a fog covering the picture. After the first 15 or 20 minutes, things do get a bit better. If you do buy it, realize that the first part of the film will have what I believe is the poorest picture quality of any Blu-ray I have probably seen to date. Later in the film things get a bit better especially in the well lit interior scenes and the outdoor scenes. Enjoy this fun film. I have for over 20 years on laser disc. .....There is an excellent special feature on the disc: The Cutting Edge: Reflections from the Ice. It was produced in 2006 and provides some interesting insight into the actors and the film's production. In my opinion, the film gets a rating of 5 but the Blu-ray quality gets a 1. Sure needs a remaster which, sadly enough, probably won't happen.

history.title: Disraeli
history.text: George Arliss plays Prime Minister Disraeli with his usual electric presence on screen. He's wonderfully human, wily and tender, scheming and charming, often charmingly scheming. The main premise is the acquiring of the Suez Canal so Britain can become a major imperialist power in India. The film suffers from two problems. First, the sound is rather muffled and requires subtitles. The second is that it often seems like a filmed play. Other than that, it's worth seeing for Arliss' performance, which won him an Academy Award, although I prefer his other performances in The Man Who Played God and The Millionaire.

history.title: The House Of Rothschild DVD 1934 Boris Karloff George Arliss
history.text: This movie tells the story of the Rothschilds and their motivations for becoming the wealthiest banking family in Europe. George Arliss gives his usual electrifying performance in a dual role as the head of the family and also his eldest son. We watch him as he and the Jews experience caustic anti-Semitism and his efforts to combat it with his wealth and power. The plot is fast-paced and thrilling as Nathan Rothschild manages to outwit his nemesis, played by a diabolical Boris Karloff. Above all, I liked Nathan's belief that with great wealth comes great responsibility and the duty to use it to achieve peace.

history.title: Cardinal Richelieu
history.text: George Arliss delivers his usual fabulous, magnetic presence as Cardinal Richelieu, the shadow behind the throne of King Louis XIII. As in Arliss' other movies, it's thrilling to watch him outfox his adversaries, whether it be the King's advisor, the Queen, or the feudal lords. I especially loved his first appearance in the King's bedroom when he simply stands there, silent and menacing. You can really believe Arliss is Richelieu, where his very name invokes terror in the hearts of people. The film has a different tone than Alexandre Dumas' novel, TheThree Musketeers, a favorite of mine, but it's as fun to watch.

history.title: Martin Scorsese's World Cinema Project No. 2: (Insiang / Mysterious Object at Noon / Revenge / Limite / Law of the Border / Taipei Story) (The Criterion Collection) [Blu-ray+DVD]
history.text: The first hour was excellent and kept my attention. Edward Yang knows how to show his characters' emotions pictorially. For example, when they feel trapped, he shows them behind bars, window frames, the interiors of cars, and elevators. City and traffic shots of Taipei are abundantly shown moving rapidly and constantly in the background and foreground while the characters seem in stasis. Moreoever, lots of corporate images have a Leviathan-like presence taking over the city and engulfing the people (a gigantic Fuji Billboard is most prominent). However, after the first hour, the film started to feel repetitive and drawn out. Its gloomy tone also began to get on my nerves. I also felt a huge weakness was the lack of chemistry between the couple, Chin and Lung. Almost from the very start, Lung didn't seem to care much about Chin - he was more absorbed in the baseball game on TV than her. Chin also didn't seem attached to Lung. There was a plot line where she even had a fling with her co-worker, which suggested she wasn't committed to Lung. When you start with relationships that are practically zero, there's not much to fall from.

history.review_title: Despite some good moments, Season 7 felt forced and rushed
history.text: Season 7 delivered some good dramatic moments. Memorable scenes for me included Jorah Mormont's cure and reunion with Dany, Theon's cowardly act jumping off the ship, and Jon's offering to return Jorah's family sword, Longclaw. I also enjoyed seeing characters we've been following through the years finally meet on screen. And yet, I couldn't help but feel that everything was rushed. Several plot developments felt either forced or simply ludicrous. Partly, it was the result of the producers' decision to limit the season to a mere seven episodes. Or, more crucially, the show no longer had GRRM's novels to rely upon as its source. Whatever the case, the quality dropped off considerably. Rather than being rushed, previous seasons after Season 3 suffered from the opposite problem. They felt overly long. All of Dany's story in Merreen was stagnant and boring. So, too, was Arya's story in Braavos. If the producers had jettisoned most of this material (i.e. Arya's thrilling trip to Braavos at the end of Season 4 being the last we saw of her until her reappearance disguised as Waldor Frey at the beginning of Season 7), they could've added more episodes in Season 7 (or Season 6 as we've just cut all the Braavos material and most of the Mereen delay). This might've prevented the story from feeling so slapdash and sloppy. Adding more time and episodes alone, however, wouldn't have have helped with some of the story flaws. For example, how ridiculous was it to take a small group of men into the North to kidnap a Wight? Or, the entire Sansa/Arya/Little Finger intrigue which seemed designed only to fool the viewer? Arya, who was once my favorite character, took a serious nosedive. And, how about Uncle Benjen coming to the rescue like that? Season 8 is reported to have 6 episodes. Even if they extended episodes, I foresee it will be plagued by the same problems as Season 7.

history.title: A Room With A View
history.review_title: Falls Short of Being a Good Movie
history.text: I first saw this 30 years ago and watched it twice. At the time, I thought I was supposed to like it because, to like it was to be sophisticated, artsy, and intellectual. Above all, there was opera in it and who was I to question high-brow culture? Thus, I went along with the crowd and praised it with my peers and the critics. Viewing it 30 years later, I still think it's a handsome production with a beautiful main actress, Helena Bonham Carter. The costumes are nice as well as the cinematography and set design. However, I don't think it's a good movie. The main problem is that the story seems to lurch like an old car, never finding its rhythm. At certain times, the scenes were cut too short, interrupted by a chapter heading. One prominent example was when George Emerson and Lucy Honeychurch converse over the river after they've just witnessed a horrific murder. George confides that they're both forever changed by this incident. What should have followed was a reaction closeup of Lucy, an expression on her face that showed her inner emotion and turmoil as she absorbed George's words. What we got was...a cut to the next chapter heading. With a gifted actress like Helena Bonham Carter, it was a wasted opportunity. What's more, I never felt I got to know any of the characters deeply. George Emerson was an enigma like the question mark he left in his room. Daniel Day-Lewis, who played Cecil, was a thoroughly unlikable prig. What did Lucy ever see in him to accept his marriage proposal? It's so unbelievable. Clearly, Cecil was not Mr. Right, but was George? Possibly. Or, possibly, what Lucy needed was more time to explore and mature and get to know herself. George and his father were very close, but absent was a heartfelt conversation between the two of them. Lucy and her brother, Freddy, were also very close, but there were no deep words between them either. Such scenes might've helped. The view from the window may be nice, but after awhile, you can forget it.

history.title: When a Woman Ascends the Stairs (The Criterion Collection) [DVD]
history.text: I like Hideko Takamine's performance as a young widow who maintains her dignity as a Ginza hostess. She's an empathetic character who helps her family despite her limited means. She's the strongest part about the movie. The main weakness, I thought, were the male characters who looked superficially different, but weren't all that distinguishable. Even the banker whom Hideko was supposed to be in love with didn't stand out for me. The same could be said about the female characters other than Hideko. The director, Mikio Naruse, has a limited range in characterization, imo. This was a competently directed film. The cinematography, staging, and lighting weren't especially noteworthy or inventive. For the full use of cinematic language, I'd strongly recommend Kenji Mizoguchi, who deals with similar themes.

history.title: T-Men (Special Edition)
history.text: What's special about this film is the cinematography. I thought the lighting was simply gorgeous. The story itself was just okay as there were a few plot holes. For example, why would the Treasury Department take such a risk and not alert Genaro's wife that he was undercover? Also, why would the Big Boss risk killing The Schemer when he knew he had the revealing book on him? I give the cinematography by John Alton five stars and the other parts a three-star rating.

history.title: Welcome To L.A.
history.review_title: Loneliness Not Enough to Save The Movie
history.text: I've watched this film twice. The first time I saw it years ago, I was impressed by the feelings of loneliness and yearning that it gave. Alan Rudolph has a talent for ambience and feeling and, maybe, it's his strongest attribute. The film's about a group of people in LA, who are lonely and searching for connection. Sexual relations and extramarital affairs aren't motivated so much by passion or love or lust as by a need for a balm for unhappiness. The second time I watched it, I liked it less and not more. The main problem is with Carroll Barber (Keith Carradine), who isn't likable. All the women are attracted to him for some inexplicable reason and, after a one-night stand, he leaves them hurt and disappointed. The film tries to portray him with great honesty, especially when he looks at the camera, but his sincerity is phony - it's just a way to bed more women. There's a moment when you think he and Lauren Hutton will have a true connection, but it leads nowhere. I liked Sissy Spacek and Lauren Hutton, but neither character was developed well. It was unclear to me what role Lauren Hutton played. She's a photographer named Nona Bruce, who documents the scenes and people in the story, but she isn't given much else to do. Richard Baskin's music provides the Chorus that holds the movie together. Some songs work well to provide moodiness and commentary on the characters, but the music gets repetitive. At the same time, the story and characters get repetitive and one-note. Sally Kellerman, Viveca Lindfors, and Geraldine Chaplin all seem like the same character by the end. Harvey Keitel is also unlikable as Kenneth Hood. He plays an ambitious assistant to Carl Barber (Denver Pyle) and he's fallen out of love with his wife, Geraldine Chaplin. Keitel, too, comes off as phony when he attempts to reconcile with his wife. He delivers lines to her that he said to his mistress, Sissy Spacek. As Geraldine Chaplin says at the beginning of the film, everyone gets deceived. Maybe that's the point of the film, but that's not enough to make this a satisfactory experience.

history.title: The Eddy Duchin Story
history.text: One of my favorite films is The Long Gray Line (1955) starring Tyrone Power and Maureen O'Hara, so I was curious to see Power in another biopic made a year later. The Eddie Duchin Story tells the life story of a Jewish-American musician and his triumphs and tragedies. Tyrone Power brings his likable charm and spirit to screen. However, he and Kim Novak play uninteresting and under-developed characters. Their courtship is presented in a montage of Central Park which is perfect, schmaltzy, and dull. By contrast, John Ford fills his characters with many details, many of them Irish, to make them memorable. He shows Irish-American identity and experience whereas this film skips over ethnicity. Almost every reference to Eddy Duchy's Jewish identity is taken out. I might add that Wikipedia describes how Mrs. Duchin was ostracized from wealthy society by marrying a Jew, but there's not a single reference to anti-semitism in this film. Both Ford's film and this one include similar tragic scenes of childbirth gone wrong. However, The Eddie Duchin Story opts to milk the tragedies of Eddy Duchin for all its worth. The music is also plentiful for those who like lounge piano music. Chopin would be rolling around in his grave if he heard this rendition of his Nocturne in E-flat Major. Victoria Shaw plays a small role as Peter Duchin's nanny and eventually Eddy Duchin's wife. It's a shame she's not more well-known since she's quite lovely and expressive. Samuel Fuller cast her in his film, The Crimson Kimono (1959), because he was impressed by her performance.

history.title: The Bitter Tea of General Yen [Blu-ray]
history.text: Barbara Stanwyck is one of my favorite actresses - she can do just about anything and I'll watch it. Here she plays a young missionary recently arrived in China to marry her childhood sweetheart. While her betrothed and she postpone their wedding to rescue orphans in a war zone, she is rescued by General Yen, who has fallen in love with her. This was a strange film. Megan can't help but be attracted to General Yen, but, at the same time, she finds his cruelty revolting. She tries to convert the General (who bears resemblance to Mephistopheles), but ends up being converted by submitting to him. Is she acting out of guilt? Does she feel naive for believing in Mah-Li and causing the General's downfall? I was surprised at Mah-Li's treachery despite being saved by General Yen and Megan. So much for loyalty. It's all a muddle at the end and General Yen's decision to commit suicide is his answer to get out of the whole mess. There's no happy ending here like the other Capra films I've seen, but only complications that ensue from two people of different races and cultures who have fallen for each other. The B&W cinematography was sumptuous and the Blu-Ray quality excellent. However, despite Stanwyck's presence and the exotic settings and props, the film was just okay. I'd recommend it for Stanwyck and Capra fans only, but it's not a must-see.

history.title: THE MIRACLE WOMAN
history.text: Barbara Stanwyck plays the daughter of a minister who seeks revenge on the hypocritical people of her parish. She teams up with a con artist and becomes a filthy-rich megachurch evangelist. Problems arise when she falls in love with a blind musician who believes in her message of faith. She also learns how hard it is to become honest after partnering with a devious man. This was the second collaboration between Stanwyck and Frank Capra. I loved the scenes between Sister Fallon and John and the dummy, Al. The scene at the beach with crashing waves was also memorable and tender. Stanwyck is wonderful playing a young woman who is naive as well as tough. The only problem I had was the ending; it felt like a deus ex machina. Hornsby, infatuated with Sister Fallon, seemed to set her free after the fire. What happened to all his threats? How was she able to join the Salvation Army with all that Hornsby held over her? Despite the ending, this was a great film. I wonder what the people who get suckered by the megachurch televangelists would think after watching this?

history.title: Landscape in the Mist
history.text: What did I just watch for two hours? Two children embark on a road trip to search for their father in Germany. It's a MacGuffin since we learn from the uncle that there is no father and that it was just a lie. The children refuse to believe it and continue on their quest. Along the way, they meet someone who helps them and someone who rapes the young girl in a terribly disturbing scene. I read that the director was influenced by Orson Welles' long take at the beginning of Touch of Evil. Here, Angelopolous makes virtually every shot in the movie using the long take. Granted, it must've taken a great deal of time and patience to get every shot right, but after awhile, I stopped being impressed and started to wonder where this was going. A giant hand emerges from the water and is carted off by a helicoptor. A tree emerges out of the mist. It was unclear to me what any of this was supposed to mean. Would it have made any difference if a tree had emerged from the water and a giant hand had emerged out of the mist? My conclusion? I thought this was a pretentious movie.

history.title: The Strange Love of Martha Ivers [DVD]
history.text: The acting talent seemed wasted in this rather dull film about a murder that took place 18 years ago. I toyed around with the idea of each of the actors switching roles. What, for example, would the film have been if Barbara Stanwyck had taken Toni's role and Kirk Douglas had played Sam? Douglas should've been cast as Sam, but this was his first movie role and no one seemed to know how best to use his talents. Also, I thought Van Heflin was more suited to the meek, devoted Walter O'Connor role. Another idea I had was to begin the film with the ending and show the rest of the film as a flashback. Not sure if those ideas would've helped, though.

history.title: The Deceivers - The Merchant Ivory Collection
history.review_title: Handsome Production and Lead Actor Is Not Enough
history.text: Before I watched this film, I considered Pierce Brosnan to be a wooden actor straight out of GQ magazine. I didn't like him as the suave Remington Steele or as James Bond. His performance in this film, to my surprise, was a step above his usual acting. Here, he plays a British officer in British-controlled India who goes undercover to infiltrate a murderous cult called the Thuggee. Their method is to strangle their victims, rob them, and bury the bodies. Brosnan slowly loses his identity and starts to get off on the killing. It's what he learns about himself that is the most disturbing part of the story. By the end, when he throws away his crucifix, you know that his old beliefs and his wife's love can't help him any longer. The production design including the costumes and period details was excellent. Unfortunately, the film never really took off. Brosnan, despite acting in maybe his best role, did not have the emotional presence to make the film moving to me. The plot also felt thin and stretched out to nearly two hours with repetitive killings and chase scenes through vegetation.

history.title: Sherlock
history.text: After Sir Arthur Conan Doyle brought Sherlock back to life in The Empty House, there were a few more good stories left but a noticeable drop in quality. It was as if the author was tired of the character or, possibly, just ran out of good ideas. The same unraveling started to occur in Season 3 of Sherlock and continued with an unpleasant and sloppy Season 4. The series jumped the shark when Charles Augustus Magnussen's would-be assassin turned out to be Mary Morstan. With the introduction of a psychopathic sister, Eurus, and her disguises as therapist, handicapped daughter, and love interest, the implausibility stretched so far that it snapped. Moreover, the horror story at Sherrinford was not entertaining like the cat-and-mouse games between Sherlock and Moriarty or Irene Adler, it was just unpleasant to watch. I was looking forward to a Season 5, but after this, it may be a good time to put the series to rest. Overall, I enjoyed the first two Seasons with the exception of "The Blind Banker". A Scandal in Belgravia was the highlight of the entire series for me.

history.title: Paths of Glory
history.text: The film does a good job showing the insanity of war and a little of what it must've been like to be in a trench during WW I. Kirk Douglas, always watchable, plays a colonel in the French army who's ordered to lead a suicide mission. As the soldiers scramble across the barbed wire and rocky terrain, I was reminded of ants. Then, I remembered their objective was to take Anthill - we're all insects here. As if to drive the point home, a soldier squashes a cockroach. The main problem is that Kirk Douglas alone wears a white hat while all the surrounding officers wear black hats. There seems to be no in-betweens. The two officers in charge are depicted as slimy and less-than-human. At one point, Douglas accuses Adolphe Menjou of being a sadistic, old man. The kangaroo court doesn't fare well either. We're meant to hate these people in power, who eat nice dinners and go off to their luxurious parties. Yes, there probably were officers like these, but were all of them? For this reason, the film, while making a strong statement about the absurdity and cruelty of war, falls short because of its simplistic characterizations.

history.title: Sleep My Love
history.text: It's hard to see what attracted Sirk to this project. Maybe it was assigned to him? It's about a rich woman, Claudette Colbert, whose husband, Don Ameche, plots to make her believe that she's mad. He plans for her to commit suicide and, after she's dead, continue living with his mistress. Plans go awry when Colbert meets and falls in love with her friend's friend, played by an amusing Robert Cummings. The cinematography is nice, but absent is Sirk's style and themes. It's pretty straightforward and runs a little too long. In Jon Halliday's book of interviews with Sirk, the director didn't have too much to say about it except that he remembered the Chinatown wedding. He also said that he wanted to emphasize Colbert's split character and believed that was the most interesting part of the story. I'm not sure what he meant by this -- her doubts about her madness? Or, her unwillingness to believe that her husband was trying to make her insane? Whatever the case, Sirk's lack of interest in the project showed.

history.title: Stay Hungry [DVD]
history.text: I watched this film because I'm a big fan of Sally Field. She plays the love interest of Jeff Bridges, who works for a real estate company intent on buying a gym to make way for an expensive high rise. The cast has a likable charm. I especially liked the chemistry between Jeff and Sally. The film is set in Alabama and retains a lot of local color including a fiddling band where Arnold Schwarzenegger (!) plays. Unfortunately, the second half isn't good. Jeff Bridges acts like a jerk at a country club party for some inexplicable reason. He's supposed to be ashamed of his friends, Sally and Arnold, because they aren't sophisticated enough, but there was no setup for this turn of character; it just came out of the blue. The plot became disjointed and tedious and I just wanted it to end. It was worth watching, especially for Sally Field and Jeff Bridges, but it's too bad the second half fell apart. Arnold is also likable although his acting range and role is limited.

Richard Pasco does an excellent job playing Brutus in this adaptation of Julius Caesar. I found him convincing as a person who agonizes over doing what he thinks is right against betraying his friend. Also, the very qualities which make him so honorable prove to be his undoing; he projects his own values and beliefs on the crowd and on Mark Antony, imagining that they'll understand why the assassins had to do what they did. Of course, Brutus should've heeded Cassius' warnings, but, just like every other piece of advice Cassius offered, didn't listen. The scenes which moved me the most were the intimate conversations between husband and wife, both Brutus' wife, Portia, and Caesar's wife, Calpurnia. I also liked the short exchanges between Brutus and his young servant, Lucius, and Brutus' tender regard for him. My sympathies, curiously, were with Brutus even though he perpetrated such a dastardly deed. I wondered why? Mark Antony and Octavius weren't likable, although they seemed to be on the right side. The only thing I didn't like about this production was that it seemed to drag in places, especially Mark Antony's funeral oration. Whether it was the fault of the production, the choice of actor, or the play itself, I'm not sure. Finally, my favorite line in all the play was said by Titinius when he discovers Cassius has killed himself. "Alas, thou hast misconstrued everything."

history.text: This is a great movie, and like all great movies, it should be available the way the director meant it to be seen, in WIDESCREEN. history.title: Poltergeist (Blu-ray Book Packaging)
history.text: I'm giving this 5 stars because I love the movie and for the nice Dig iBook packaging. However, be aware that the disc is flawed. JoBeth William's dialog is cut off at the end of scene 8, as the movie jumps to scene 9. I returned my original to Warner Bros for a new copy, and the new copy has the same flaw. So I'm guessing the only way Warner Bros will fix this issue, is if everyone who now owns a flawed copy get in touch with Warner Bros and asks for a proper release, or refuses to buy it in the first place. So here's hoping Warner Bros gets the message, and releases a proper copy.

history.review_title: Good movie, bad streaming at end
history.text: This is a very good movie about the hypocrisy of business and family. The lead gets in a financial jam, and the mistake snowballs out of control. If you like Richard Gere in a thinking man's movie, this is for you. After watching about 85% of the movie with no problems, the streaming stopped, and stuttered. I had to restart the movie 4 times, and fast forward to get past the parts I had already seen. I got an error message about my internet from Amazon, but the problem was not on my end, it was on Amazon's end. This is only the 2nd or 3rd film I've watched on Amazon, and there seems to be no option for subtitles. That is a big disappointment.

history.title: Ultimate Gangsters Collection: Classics (Little Caesar / The Public Enemy / The Petrified Forest / White Heat [Blu-ray]
history.review_title: The rise of the gangster movie!
history.text: This classic movie collection, along with the great special features that go with it, highlight the rise of the gangster movie as we now know it. Produced just after the advent of the talkies, and with no film ratings board, these movies shocked and delighted audiences. They also made stars out of James Cagney, and Edward G. Robinson. Interesting both for their history, as well as the films themselves, this is a must have collection for the film buff!

history.review_title: Production values and special effects were surprisingly good for a movie this old
history.text: Production values and special effects were surprisingly good for a movie this old. Picture quality was excellent, as well. Though this is a sci-fi movie, at it's heart, it's a morality tale-way ahead of it's time. How to pick 40 people from all the citizens of the US to populate another planet when the earth is doomed? And the way the rest of the populace reacts to that decision. This film was much better then expected.

history.review_title: A good British production that left out a US contribution
history.text: This is a very interesting 2 part British program about the history of code breakers. However, they left out a contribution by the US Navy in WWII. That was the capture of U-505 off the cost of Africa. A specially trained crew boarded the U-Boat after repeated depth charging forced the boat to the surface. The German's tried to scuttle the boat, but the US Navy crew shut the petcocks, and disarmed demolition charges. She was then towed 1700 miles to Bermuda, and her crew interned in the US. The operation was top secret, and the German government never knew that the US was now in possession of their code books, and Enigma machine. After doing some fact checking on Wikipedia, I found that the program also left out a Canadian U-Boat capture. Maybe this was because the allies in Benchley Park were already able to decode most Enigma messages before these captures took place. I noticed the omission because years ago I had read about the capture of U-505, and had also seen it in the Chicago Museum of Science And Industry.

history.title: Gridiron Gang - Blu-ray
history.text: This is a very good movie, but Mill Creek Entertainment should not be allowed to release any more Sony films.. Having no menu, or special features is bad enough, but NO SUBTITLES? The original Sony release featured 9 different subtitles-count them-9! And a few special features, as well. And that release is actually selling for a bit less on Amazon right now. It's the one with "The Rock" standing in a black shirt in front of the team. And it's the one that is reviewed on blu-ray.com in all it's glory, leading you to think that this version has the same features. The way these blu-rays are released in different versions by different companies, and confusing the hell out of the consumer makes me want to split nails! Is it the "extended version", or the "directors cut"? How many times are we going to be asked to double or triple dip, to get the "ultimate version"? You sure need to read the fine print when you buy a blu-ray now a days!

history.review_title: ... one star is not for the series-the show is great! The one star is for the price of ...
history.text: The one star is not for the series-the show is great! The one star is for the price of this set. Why spend 184.00 on 9 seasons, when you can buy all 10 seasons at the price of 10.00 each? Which, of course, only adds up to 100.00. Even if you want to pre-order season 11 at 39.98, it's still a hell of a lot cheaper than 184.00. Can you spell RIP OFF?

Great production for both Civil War, and medical history buff. It manages to show the views (right or wrong) and circumstances of both sides of the conflict. Also features great sets. I'm looking forward to season 2.
